# UI fonts

**Rule.** Draw with `font_ui_*`, never `lv_font_montserrat_*`. The faces are generated by `scripts/make-ui-font.sh` over `0x20-0x7F,0xA1-0x17F,0x401,0x410-0x44F,0x451,0x2022` (Latin-1, Latin Extended-A, Russian Cyrillic, bullet) plus exactly the Chinese characters the source uses.

**Why.** LVGL draws a missing glyph as a blank box and logs nothing. The built-in faces are ASCII only and switched off in `lv_conf.h` so the mistake does not link.

**How.**
- A new Chinese character: `bash scripts/make-ui-font.sh`, then `python3 scripts/gen-font-range.py`, and commit the faces.
- A new script (alphabet): widen `TEXT_RANGE` in `make-ui-font.sh`, regenerate, and update this rule in the same commit.
- `0xA0` (no-break space) is left out on purpose: a no-break space with no glyph is visible.
- `check-ui-fonts.py` fails on a string outside the range; `check-generated.py` re-runs the generator (needs `pio pkg install` in `firmware/` once).
